inputs: zero-based index of last callback for operation 1/2

semantics: HIA controls only per-validation callback order and stop/continue decisions. Rust owns construction of each isolated Policy, callback execution, RuleMatch/RuleRef Debug, shlex rendering, error locations and actual Starlark parsing.
The host executes exactly the callback indicated by opcode 1 or 2, then invokes the reducer once with operation 1 or 2 and observed=0/1; it must never prefetch or memoize callbacks.
For opcode 2 or 4 with append_unmatched_before_next_callback=1, the host must render and append the just-observed unmatched positive before executing any later matching callback or RuleRef Debug.

Opcode 3 demands immediate first-negative error rendering (matched RuleMatch Debug first, then offending example). Opcode 4 demands all RuleRef Debug only after every positive callback and required unmatched-example rendering.
The host maintains authoritative monotonic state across calls; this pure HIA function does not authenticate the caller-supplied cursor or mismatch count against a previous response.
Each pending validation uses a fresh state and its own Rust-owned Policy; the first failing validation aborts later validations and attaches the original location.
All validation paths finish before a 40-byte write. Short/invalid returns must leave the full caller output untouched; short-output is checked after exact input length.
